references.text: Describes the use of red-dyed ram skins and tachash skins as a covering over the tabernacle, which is the practical purpose of the materials mentioned in 25:5.
Repeats the list of materials that the people were to bring, including red-dyed ram skins, tachash skins, and acacia wood.
States that the people actually brought red-dyed ram skins and tachash skins as offerings for the tabernacle.
Describes how red-dyed ram skins and tachash skins were used to make coverings over the tabernacle.
Mentions the covering of red-dyed ram skins and the covering of tachash skins as part of the completed work on the tabernacle.
Tachash skins are used as a covering over the ark of the covenant during transport in the wilderness.
Tachash skins are used to cover the lampstand and its utensils during transport.
Mentions the covering of tachash skins as part of the tabernacle's equipment that the sons of Gershon were to carry.
Acacia wood (shittim) is mentioned in connection with the rebuilding of the temple in Ezekiel's vision, linking it to the materials of the tabernacle.
